note: Decoder populates operands from x86OperandSets; some operand slots may remain kInvalid if the instruction encoding is incomplete or malformed.

code: MCInst_clear(MI); for (i = 0; i < x86Inst->numOperands; i++) { if (x86Inst->operands[i].encoding != ENCODING_NONE) translateOperand(MI, &x86Inst->operands[i], insn); }
note: translateInstruction clears MI (resets size to 0 but does not re-initialize Operand Kind fields), then iterates only operands with ENCODING_NONE check. If translateRMMemory fails partway, fewer than 5 sub-operands are created.
translateRMMemory creates 5 operands (base, scale, index, disp, segment). If the instruction encoding causes early exit, some sub-operand slots remain kInvalid with uninitialized ImmVal.

printMemReference accesses operand at offset 1 (ScaleAmt) via MCOperand_getImm without checking MCOperand_isReg or MCOperand_isImm first. If that slot is kInvalid, the ImmVal field is uninitialized, causing a use-of-uninitialized-value read.
printInstruction dispatches to printMemReference for memory operands. The uninitialized ImmVal is read and printed, triggering the MSan/UBsan violation.
